65437-beware-the-usurpers.title: Beware The Usurpers
65437-beware-the-usurpers.creator: Unknown
65437-beware-the-usurpers.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. There was an old army officer, leathered and permanently tanned by decades of the dreadful Indian sun; he wore a short grizzled mustache and a stern, rather stuffy expression. There was a man of about fifty who could not have been anything but a physician, so scrubbed and competent he seemed. There was a youngish fellow with only one arm, and another whose dark glasses sheltered sightless scar-pitted hollows.

68446-the-soup-and-sauce-book.title: Soup and Sauce Book
68446-the-soup-and-sauce-book.creator: Elizabeth Douglas
68446-the-soup-and-sauce-book.description: A book by Elizabeth Douglas. _Utensils._--Of special utensils for making soup, porcelain-lined sauce-pans are the most satisfactory, and should always be used if possible. There is nothing so good or clean as the large French _pot au feu_, which can be bought in Soho. Earthenware sauce-pans are also good.

arxiv-2107-00040.creator: Keller VandeBogert
arxiv-2107-00040.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Keller VandeBogert. In this paper, we study conditions guaranteeing that a product of ideals defines a Golod ring. We show that for a 3 3 -dimensional regular local ring (or 3 3 -variable polynomial ring) ( R , 𝔪 ) (R,\mathfrak{m}) , the ideal I ​ 𝔪 I\mathfrak{m} always defines a Golod ring for any proper ideal I ⊂ R I\subset R .

arxiv-2205-13074.title: Sample-efficient verification of continuously-parameterized quantum gates for small quantum processors
arxiv-2205-13074.creator: Ryan Shaffer, Hang Ren, Emiliia Dyrenkova, Christopher G. Yale, Daniel S. Lobser, Ashlyn D. Burch, Matthew N. H. Chow, Melissa C. Revelle, Susan M. Clark, Hartmut Häffner
arxiv-2205-13074.description: Abstract Most near-term quantum information processing devices will not be capable of implementing quantum error correction and the associated logical quantum gate set. Instead, quantum circuits will be implemented directly using the physical native gate set of the device. These native gates often have a parameterization (e.g., rotation angles) which provide the ability to perform a continuous range of operations.

arxiv-2211-01966.title: MarginNCE: Robust Sound Localization with a Negative Margin
arxiv-2211-01966.creator: Sooyoung Park*, Arda Senocak*, Joon Son Chung
arxiv-2211-01966.description: Abstract The goal of this work is to localize sound sources in visual scenes with a self-supervised approach. Contrastive learning in the context of sound source localization leverages the natural correspondence between audio and visual signals where the audio-visual pairs from the same source are assumed as positive, while randomly selected pairs are negatives.

arxiv-2310-07205.creator: S.-X. Yi, C.-W. Wang, X. Shao, R. Moradi, H. Gao, B. Zhang, S.-L. Xiong, S.-N. Zhang, W.-J. Tan, J.-C. Liu, W.-C. Xue, Y.-Q. Zhang, C. Zheng, Y. Wang, P. Zhang, Z.-H. An, C. arxiv-2310-07205.description: Abstract The second brightest GRB in history, GRB230307A, provides an ideal laboratory to study the mechanism of GRB prompt emission thanks to its extraordinarily high photon statistics and its single episode activity . Here we demonstrate that the rapidly variable components of its prompt emission compose an overall broad single pulse-like profile.

arxiv-2410-17416.title: Modulation leading to frequency downshifting of water waves in the vicinity of the Benjamin-Feir transition
arxiv-2410-17416.creator: Daniel J. Ratliff, Olga Trichtchenko, Thomas J. Bridges
arxiv-2410-17416.description: Abstract For Stokes waves in finite depth within the neighbourhood of the Benjamin-Feir stability transition, there are two families of periodic waves, one modulationally unstable and the other stable. In this paper we show that these two families can be joined by a heteroclinic connection, which manifests in the fluid as a travelling front.

arxiv-2412-13308.title: Generalized Scattering Matrix Formulation and its Relationship with TARC and Maximum Power Transfer Theorem
arxiv-2412-13308.creator: Majid Manteghi
arxiv-2412-13308.description: Abstract This paper presents a generalized framework for analyzing arbitrary passive matching networks using a Thévenin-Helmholtz equivalent circuit. Unlike prior formulations, which impose restrictive assumptions such as diagonal impedance matrices, the proposed approach accommodates arbitrary multiport networks, including interconnected and non-diagonal impedance configurations.

arxiv-2501-12579.title: Classical and quantum algorithms for characters of the symmetric group
arxiv-2501-12579.creator: Sergey Bravyi, David Gosset, Vojtech Havlicek, Louis Schatzki
arxiv-2501-12579.description: Abstract Characters of irreducible representations are ubiquitous in group theory. However, computing characters of some groups such as the symmetric group S n S_{n} is a challenging problem known to be #P-hard in the worst case. Here we describe a Matrix Product State (MPS) algorithm for characters of S n S_{n} .

arxiv-2503-19208.title: Spinoptics in the Kerr Spacetime: Polarized Wave Scattering
arxiv-2503-19208.creator: Valeri P. Frolov, Alex Koek
arxiv-2503-19208.description: Abstract We study propagation of high-frequency electromagnetic and gravitational waves in the gravitational field of a rotating black hole. Due to the interaction of the spin of the field with the spacetime curvature, the standard geometric optics approximation that is used for obtaining the approximate high-frequency solutions of the wave equation should be modified.

We prove that planes and spheres are the only stationary surfaces for E α E_{\alpha} with constant Gauss curvature.

arxiv-2508-20391.description: Abstract Traditionally, fast solar wind is considered to originate in solar source regions that are continuously open to the heliosphere. In contrast, slow solar wind is considered to originate in source regions that are only intermittently open to the heliosphere.

arxiv-2509-18289.title: Homophily in Complex Networks: Measures, Models, and Applications
arxiv-2509-18289.creator: Akrati Saxena 1 , Gaurav Kumar 2 and Chandrakala Meena 2
arxiv-2509-18289.description: Abstract Homophily, the tendency of individuals to connect with others who share similar attributes, is a defining feature of social networks. Understanding how groups interact, both within and across, is crucial for uncovering the dynamics of network evolution and the emergence of structural inequalities in these network.

pmc-10532318.title: Differences in Male-Killing Rickettsia Bacteria between Lineages of the Invasive Gall-Causing Pest Leptocybe invasa
pmc-10532318.creator: Xin Peng, Hantang Wang, Zhende Yang, Rosemarie C Rosell
pmc-10532318.description: Simple SummaryThis study compared the differences in symbiotic bacteria between the A and B lineages of the Leptocybe invasa, so as to provide a reference for the scientific control of the pest.Abstract(1) Background: Leptocybe invasa (Hymenoptera: Eulophidae) is a global invasive pest that seriously damages eucalyptus plants and has caused serious harm to forestry production in many countries.

pmc-10619208.title: Recent advances in the understanding of tubal ectopic pregnancy
pmc-10619208.creator: Heather C Flanagan, W Colin Duncan, Chih-Jen Lin, Norah Spears, Andrew W Horne
pmc-10619208.description: Ectopic pregnancy (EP) is described as the implantation of an embryo outside the normal uterine cavity. It most commonly occurs in the fallopian tube, hence termed a tubal ectopic pregnancy (tEP). It is a gynaecological emergency and remains the leading cause of direct maternal mortality related to the first trimester of pregnancy worldwide.

pmc-11474718.title: Quality and completeness of, and spin in reporting of, pilot and feasibility studies in hip and knee arthroplasty: a protocol for a methodological survey
pmc-11474718.creator: Zinnia Chung, Lawrence Mbuagbaw, Lipalo Mokete, Mohit Bhandari, Lehana Thabane
pmc-11474718.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). AbstractIntroduction Pilot or feasibility trials examine the feasibility, viability and recruitment potential of larger, main trials. Specifically, a pilot trial can be instrumental in identifying methodological issues essential to the development of an effective research protocol. However, numerous studies published as pilot or feasibility studies have demonstrated notable inconsistencies in the nature of information reported, resulting in poor-quality and incomplete reporting.

pmc-11507342.title: Health Risks Associated with Adopting New-Generation Disposable Products Among Young Adults Who Use E-Cigarettes
pmc-11507342.creator: Shuyao Ran, James J Yang, Megan E Piper, Hsien-Chang Lin, Anne Buu, Paul B Tchounwou
pmc-11507342.description: New-generation disposable e-cigarettes have become increasingly popular among young adults in the USA since the FDA’s partial flavor ban. This study aims to examine longitudinal changes in health risks among young adults who adopted these novel products, as well as the health effects of device types beyond the effects of other important e-cigarette characteristics.

pmc-11604175.title: Efficacy and Clinical Utility of Sodium Fluoride Tubes Versus Serum Tubes for Blood Glucose Estimation
pmc-11604175.creator: Disha Daimane, Sharbari Basu
pmc-11604175.description: Introduction: Precise and accurate measurement of blood glucose is the key factor in both the diagnosis and effective management of diabetes mellitus. The blood glucose levels are influenced by the time interval between sample collection and measurement as glycolysis continues to take place in the blood cells. Laboratories make efforts to minimize this change.

pmc-12534714.title: Potential and Limitations of Large Language Models for Medical Literature Analysis: A Preliminary Investigation
pmc-12534714.creator: Takahiro Kamihara, Takuya Omura, Atsuya Shimizu
pmc-12534714.description: ObjectiveWhile Large Language Models (LLMs) show great promise for various medical applications, their black-box nature and the difficulty of reproducing results have been noted as significant challenges. In contrast, conventional text mining is a well-established methodology, yet its mastery remains time-consuming.

pmc-12546575.title: Genistein enhances anti-PD-1 efficacy in melanoma by suppressing regulatory T cell differentiation and activity
pmc-12546575.creator: Fei Mo, Min Hong, Xiao Chen, Qiye Wang, Chao Dong
pmc-12546575.description: The accumulation of regulatory T cells (Tregs) in the tumor microenvironment is a key factor for immunosuppression and immune escape of cancer cells. Genistein is a natural isoflavonoid in soybeans, possessing a wide range of pharmacological bioactivities. However, the immunomodulatory potential of genistein remains largely unexplored.

pmc-12729996.title: Addressing Heterogeneity in Equine PRP Therapies: A Scoping Review of Methods, Evidence, and Commercial Validation
pmc-12729996.creator: Jorge U Carmona, Catalina López, David Argüelles, Chris W Rogers
pmc-12729996.description: Simple SummaryPlatelet-rich plasma (PRP) is a treatment derived from a horse’s own blood that is used to help heal injuries. However, the way vets prepare PRP varies greatly, making it difficult to compare results between studies and know which method works best. This review collected and analyzed all the available scientific studies on how PRP is made for horses.

pmc-12748306.title: Assessing effectiveness and skill transferability in multi-platform simulated training for robotic surgical skills: a systematic review
pmc-12748306.creator: Wai Miu Emma Liu, Katy-Anne Burr, Charvi Dave, Callum Pearse, Yang Li, Julien Quarez, Alejandro Granados, Ben Challacombe, Prokar Dasgupta, Nicholas Raison
pmc-12748306.description: With more robotic platforms approved for clinical use, interest in assessing skill transferability has increased. Skill transfer has yet to be studied amongst trainees in early stages of robotic training. This systematic review evaluated skill transferability of robotic platforms amongst trainees in simulated settings. The systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines.

pmc-12861742.title: Global disease and economic burden of main mycobacterial infections in the working-age population from 1990 to 2021 with a forecast to 2045
pmc-12861742.creator: Jiaxu Gu, Jiaming Wang, Long Zhong, Bingcheng Lu, Hongqiang Xie, Bo Yu, Yang Guo
pmc-12861742.description: Highlights•Declining Leprosy, Rising TB in Elderly: Leprosy prevalence dropped (14.426–5.942/100,000), while TB cases increased in older adults (50–64 years).•Socioeconomic Gaps Drive Burden: Low-income regions face higher leprosy burdens (CI: −0.35); health spending (ρ = −0.557) and UHC (ρ = −0.785) reduce disparities.•Drug Resistance Threatens Progress: MDR/XDR-TB and HIV co-infections challenge gains; targeted funding and global cooperation urged.

pmc-12984843.title: Exploring Adipose Tissue Complexity Through Omics Approaches: Implications for Health and Disease
pmc-12984843.creator: Rajaa Sebaa
pmc-12984843.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Omics revealed diverse adipocytes and their molecular structures and dynamics.Omics showed ATs coordinate whole-body metabolism via genes, proteins and metabolites. What are the implications of the main findings? Omics could identify ATs-derived molecules as predictors of metabolic health.Omics may enable precision modulation of adipocyte subtypes to potentially treat metabolic disorders.

pmc-13321359.title: Disparity between Post-thaw Survival and Functional Integrity of Vitrified-thawed Oocytes from Obese Mice
pmc-13321359.creator: Sandhya Kumari, Aparna Chelvi, Vanishree Vasave Madhvacharya, Aishwarya Ashok, Mouna Bannur Karunakara, Yashas Kiran Ninjoor, Jyolsna Ponnaratta Kunhiraman, Amrutha Nedumbrakkad Kunnath, Keerthana Karunakar Poojary, Sneha Guruprasad Kalthur, Satish Kumar Adiga, Guruprasad Kalthur
pmc-13321359.description: ObjectiveObesity in women is known to be associated with compromised ovarian function. The oocytes are characterized by elevated cytoplasmic oxidative stress and poor cytoplasmic organization under such conditions, which might affect their tolerance to exogenous stresses such as the freeze-thaw process. This study investigates the cryosusceptibility of oocytes derived from mice with high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity.

pmc-13327704.title: Efficacy, Safety, and Cost‐Effectiveness of Reduced versus Full Initial Doses of Androgen Receptor Signaling Inhibitors in Non‐Metastatic Castration‐Resistant Prostate Cancer: A Multicenter Retrospective Study
pmc-13327704.creator: Himawari Asanuma, Naoki Fujita, Shumon Kato, Yohei Kawashima, Masanao Shinohara, Ryuji Tabata, Fumiya Yoneyama, Ryuma Tanaka, Takuya Oishi, Hikari Miura, Kyo Togashi, Kazutaka Okita, Hirotaka Horiguchi, Toshikazu Tanaka, Daisuke Noro, Yuichiro Suzuki, Satoshi Sato, Chikara Ohyama, Shingo Hatakeyama
pmc-13327704.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThe introduction of novel androgen receptor signaling inhibitors (ARSIs) has substantially transformed the systemic treatment landscape for non‐metastatic castration‐resistant prostate cancer (nmCRPC). Unfortunately, ARSI therapy is associated with considerable adverse events (AEs) and high medical costs. Dose reduction has been proposed as a potential strategy to improve tolerability and reduce costs; however, the efficacy, safety, and cost‐effectiveness of reduced‐dose ARSIs in patients with nmCRPC remain unclear.MethodsThis multicenter retrospective study included 251 patients with nmCRPC who underwent ARSI therapy.

uslaw-usc-t43-s475.title: 43 U.S.C. § 475 — Annual installments on entries and contracts prior to August 13, 1914
uslaw-usc-t43-s475.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t43-s475.description: United States Code, Title 43 (Public Lands); Chapter 12 (Reclamation And Irrigation Of Lands By Federal Government); Subchapter IX (Construction Charges). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Any person whose land or entry, prior to August 13, 1914, became subject to the terms and conditions of the reclamation law shall pay the construction charge, or the portion of the construction charge remaining unpaid.
